name: Rich Black (FOGRA39)
lede: Rich Black (FOGRA39) names a print-industry black calibrated to FOGRA's standard for glossy or matte coated paper.

sections.title: From a printing term to a swatch
sections.body:
"Rich black" is a printing term for an ink mixture of solid black over one or more of the other CMYK inks, giving a darker, denser result than black ink alone [1]. FOGRA, a German printing-research body, publishes registered characterization data sets describing how ink behaves on specific papers under ISO offset-printing conditions [2]. FOGRA39 describes gloss or matte coated paper at 115 grams per square meter, and is one of the most common default print profiles in design software [2]. The swatch is a flat screen approximation of that printing condition, not a measured ink sample [1][2].

Its closest sibling is [[rich-black-fogra29]], the equivalent standard for uncoated paper, and both sit near plain [[black]] on screen [1].

It also sits close to the generic near-blacks [[near-black]] and [[smoky-black]], both read as almost the same color [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In the ColorHub painting archive this near-black hue appears in 3,188 of 23,781 paintings, about 13.4 percent, the most common of the dark neutrals checked in this project, as photographed [3]. It peaks around the 1560s, and Francisco Jover y Casanova, Nicolaes Maes and Frans van Mieris use it far more than the archive average relative to their output [3]. These are computed color matches on varnished, photographed canvases, not pigment identifications [3].

questions.q: What paper does the FOGRA39 characterization data set describe?
True or false: rich black means solid black ink with no other CMYK ink underneath it.

openers: Rich Black (FOGRA39) is the most common near-black match among the dark neutrals checked here.
